primitives.name: Initial Distribution Optimality
primitives.verbatim_quote: 88 RISK, UNCERTAINTY, AND PROFIT tions as to the workings of the process itself 1 that the initial situation, the distribution of goods before the exchanges commenced, was the best possible (i.e., either absolutely ideal or absolutely beyond human power to modify).
primitives.assumptions: The pre-exchange allocation is either globally optimal or unalterable by human action.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When human intervention alters initial conditions, optimality becomes a hypothesis rather than a given.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's prior belief over resource distributions; GSE models deviation from this baseline via state transition functions.
layer2.telemetry: Observable variance in post-trade allocations relative to pre-trade idealized distributions.

primitives.name: Free Exchange Redistribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: All that is true (and stated baldly it is little better than a truisin) is that free exchange tends toward that redistribution of goods which is the most satisfactory all around of any that can be obtained by voluntary consent all around.
primitives.assumptions: Voluntary consent leads to Pareto-efficient redistribution among participants.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when coercion or asymmetric information distorts consent.

layer2.mapping: GSI infers utility-weighted redistribution probabilities; GSE simulates convergence to equilibrium through iterative bilateral trades.
layer2.telemetry: Entropy reduction in trade surplus distribution across agents.

primitives.name: Ideal Exchange Value Equality
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is self-evident that in ideal exchange the quantities exchanged are equal in value terms, and there is no chance for anything like a "profit" to arise.
primitives.assumptions: Perfect information and symmetric valuation lead to zero-profits in idealized markets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Occurs only under full rationality and complete market transparency.

layer2.mapping: GSI models profit-free equilibria using symmetric information entropy; GSE encodes this as a fixed-point in dynamic pricing algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Absence of arbitrage opportunities in simulated or observed transactions.

primitives.name: Intercommunication Imperfection
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is a familiar fact that in consequence of imperfect intercommunication appreciably different prices for the same commodity may obtain at different points in the general market area.
primitives.assumptions: Market inefficiencies stem from delayed or incomplete information propagation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Price divergence increases with communication latency and agent heterogeneity.

layer2.mapping: GSI quantifies information lag via cross-market correlation decay; GSE models price adjustment delays as stochastic drift in state-space.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-regional price spread volatility and time-lagged correlation metrics.

The foundational structure of exchange theory hinges on the tension between idealized equilibrium and real-world imperfections. The first primitive, 'initial distribution optimality', establishes a baseline where the starting allocation is either optimal or immutable—a premise that underpins normative economic models. This is dual to GSI’s Bayesian prior over resource states, which assumes an underlying truth that can be approximated but never fully known. The second primitive, 'free exchange redistribution', posits that voluntary trade moves towards Pareto improvements, forming a core principle for GSI’s belief updating on welfare outcomes and GSE’s simulation of convergent trade paths. The third, 'ideal exchange value equality', asserts that in perfect conditions, no profit arises—this maps directly to GSI’s zero-profit equilibrium states and GSE’s fixed-point logic in pricing engines. Finally, 'intercommunication imperfection' introduces a key failure mode: when information flows are incomplete, prices diverge, creating exploitable inefficiencies. This drives both GSI’s uncertainty quantification and GSE’s adaptive response protocols. Together, these primitives form a layered epistemic lattice: from static priors to dynamic feedback loops, each layer reflects increasing complexity in modeling bounded rationality and emergent behavior.
